findings.finding: D11 says 'the guard that needs a character after the backslash stays'. No such guard exists: `parseFormat` tests `format[index + 1] === "$" || === "|"`, which is simply false at the end of the string, so a trailing `\` falls through to the literal. I ran the parser at HEAD: `"tail\\"` yields the literal `tail\`. Once the condition becomes 'any character', the trailing-backslash case has no decision: `format[index + 1]` is `undefined` and the naive edit appends `undefined`. Neither D11 nor the statusline delta's scenarios ('`a\b`', '`$idle\m`') says what a format ending in `\` renders.
